provenance.authorship: Thirty-two compact chess compositions were newly composed for this Nschess candidate on 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-10 from chess rules and sparse piece arrangements. No game, book, puzzle collection, or third-party puzzle database was consulted or adapted.
provenance.rightsNote: Candidate-authored content, not sourced from the existing Lichess-derived practice collection. Organizational ownership should be confirmed before public launch; this file makes no third-party rights claim.

puzzles.title: Close the corner
puzzles.prompt: Black's king is boxed in. Find any legal move that checkmates now.
hints: Use your queen and king together.
Look for a queen move that covers h7 and g8 while your king protects the queen.
puzzles.explanation: The king and queen work as a team: the queen closes the escape squares while the king protects the mating square. Any legal checkmate in one is accepted.
puzzles.authorNote: Original three-piece mating composition; open objective accepts every legal mate-in-one alternative.

puzzles.title: Mirror the net
puzzles.prompt: The same mating idea appears on the other wing. Find any checkmate in one.
hints: Check the king's available flight squares.
A queen move on the seventh rank can be protected by your king.
puzzles.explanation: Bring the queen close enough to seal the corner, with your king guarding the checking square. Any legal checkmate in one is accepted.
puzzles.authorNote: Original mirrored mating composition; no external position was used as a template.

puzzles.title: Black-side finish
puzzles.prompt: You are playing Black. Find any legal move that checkmates White now.
hints: The white king is on the edge.
Use the queen while keeping the mating square protected by your king.
puzzles.explanation: A close queen move works because the black king protects the queen and the edge removes escape squares. Any legal checkmate in one is accepted.
puzzles.authorNote: Original black-to-move mating composition.

puzzles.title: Hold the mating square
puzzles.prompt: The black king is trapped on the opposite edge. Find any checkmate in one.
hints: Your king is already close enough to help.
Look for a queen move that the king protects.
puzzles.explanation: Keep the queen safe with king support while taking away every flight square. Any legal checkmate in one is accepted.
puzzles.authorNote: Original reflected mating composition.

puzzles.title: Royal fork
puzzles.prompt: Give check with your knight and attack the queen at the same time.
hints: A knight can attack two distant targets at once.
Find a checking knight jump that also attacks e8.
puzzles.explanation: The knight checks the king on h7 while attacking the queen on e8. The king must answer the check, leaving the queen attacked.
puzzles.authorNote: Original fork composition; every legal checking knight move that attacks the queen is accepted.

puzzles.title: Fork across the board
puzzles.prompt: Find a checking knight move that also attacks the queen.
hints: Look for a knight jump near the black king.
The destination should attack both a7 and d8.
puzzles.explanation: A knight check on a7 also attacks the queen on d8. The king has to move first, so the queen remains under attack.
puzzles.authorNote: Original horizontally reflected fork composition.

puzzles.title: Fork from Black's side
puzzles.prompt: As Black, check the king and attack the white queen with one knight move.
hints: The knight can attack the king and queen together.
Look for a checking jump that reaches a2 and d1.
puzzles.explanation: The knight checks the king on a2 and attacks the queen on d1. Answering the check leaves the queen attacked.
puzzles.authorNote: Original black-to-move fork composition, reflected and color-swapped from the author's own board setup.

puzzles.title: Find the checking fork
puzzles.prompt: Find a checking knight move that attacks the queen as well.
hints: The knight is central; search its checks.
The fork should attack h2 and e1.
puzzles.explanation: The knight checks the king on h2 while attacking the queen on e1. The king must move, leaving the queen attacked.
puzzles.authorNote: Original edge-of-board fork composition.

puzzles.title: Seal the back rank
puzzles.prompt: As Black, use rook and king together to finish the cornered king.
hints: The white king is close to the corner.
A rook check along the fifth rank leaves no flight squares.
puzzles.explanation: The rook seals the fifth rank while the black king takes away the remaining flight squares. The engine confirms this is the unique mate.
puzzles.authorNote: New sparse rook-mate composition; one legal mating move and multiple legal alternatives were verified.

puzzles.title: A rook on the second
puzzles.prompt: White to move: find the rook move that leaves no escape.
hints: The black king is boxed near the edge.
The rook can cross the second rank and check on h2.
puzzles.explanation: The rook checks along the h-file while the white king covers the nearby escape squares. This is the only mate in one.
puzzles.authorNote: New sparse rook-mate composition; one legal mating move and multiple legal alternatives were verified.

puzzles.title: Queen to the h-file
puzzles.prompt: As Black, find the queen move that mates beside the king.
hints: The white king has very little room.
Bring the queen across the fifth rank.
puzzles.explanation: The queen gives a close check and the white king has no legal reply. The mating move is unique.
puzzles.authorNote: New sparse queen-mate composition; one legal mating move and multiple legal alternatives were verified.

puzzles.title: The rook climbs
puzzles.prompt: Black to move: lift the rook to the back rank for mate.
hints: The white king is restricted by its edge.
The rook can check up the f-file.
puzzles.explanation: The rook's file check is supported by the black king, leaving the white king without a legal square or capture. There is one mate in one.
puzzles.authorNote: New sparse rook-mate composition; one legal mating move and multiple legal alternatives were verified.

puzzles.title: A rook across the rank
puzzles.prompt: White to move: close the king's last flight route.
hints: The black king is already near the edge.
Slide the rook across the fifth rank.
puzzles.explanation: The rook gives a lateral check and the white king covers the remaining flight squares. This is the unique mate.
puzzles.authorNote: New sparse rook-mate composition; one legal mating move and multiple legal alternatives were verified.

puzzles.title: Close the first rank
puzzles.prompt: Black to move: trap the white king on the first rank.
hints: The white king is already on the edge.
The rook can descend the d-file while your king controls nearby squares.
puzzles.explanation: The rook checks along the first rank while the black king blocks the remaining escape. Find the unique mate.
puzzles.authorNote: New sparse rook-mate composition; one legal mating move and multiple legal alternatives were verified.

puzzles.title: Guard the corner
puzzles.prompt: Black to move: finish the king trapped beside the edge.
hints: Your king controls the b-file escape squares.
The rook can give a protected check on the first rank.
puzzles.explanation: The rook checks along the first rank while the black king seals the remaining flight squares. The mating move is unique.
puzzles.authorNote: New sparse rook-mate composition; one legal mating move and multiple legal alternatives were verified.

puzzles.title: Queen beside the king
puzzles.prompt: Black to move: find the queen's close checkmate.
hints: The white king is on the h-file.
Place the queen on h2 to deliver the final check.
puzzles.explanation: The queen delivers a close check and the black king takes away every escape. This is the only mate.
puzzles.authorNote: New sparse queen-mate composition; one legal mating move and multiple legal alternatives were verified.

puzzles.title: The rook's final step
puzzles.prompt: White to move: bring the rook down for mate.
hints: The black king is in the corner.
The rook can check on the first rank while your king controls the escape.
puzzles.explanation: The first-rank check leaves no legal response because the white king controls the flight squares. Find the unique mate.
puzzles.authorNote: New sparse rook-mate composition; one legal mating move and multiple legal alternatives were verified.

puzzles.title: Across the back rank
puzzles.prompt: White to move: find the rook's long checkmate.
hints: The black king is cornered on a1.
The rook can travel across the eighth rank.
puzzles.explanation: The rook checks down the a-file and the corner leaves no escape. This is the unique mate in one.
puzzles.authorNote: New sparse rook-mate composition; one legal mating move and multiple legal alternatives were verified.

puzzles.title: Cut off the third rank
puzzles.prompt: Black to move: seal the white king against the edge.
hints: The white king is on h1.
A rook move along the third rank gives check.
puzzles.explanation: The rook checks down the h-file while the black king controls the available flight squares. The engine confirms a single mating move.
puzzles.authorNote: New sparse rook-mate composition; one legal mating move and multiple legal alternatives were verified.

puzzles.title: Finish on the eighth
puzzles.prompt: White to move: find the rook check the king cannot answer.
hints: The black king is restricted by your king.
The rook can rise to h8 with check.
puzzles.explanation: The rook's eighth-rank check is supported by the white king, and Black has no legal reply. There is exactly one mate in one.
puzzles.authorNote: New sparse rook-mate composition; one legal mating move and multiple legal alternatives were verified.

puzzles.title: Cross the long diagonal
puzzles.prompt: White to move: check the king and attack the queen with one knight jump.
hints: The king and queen are close together.
Find the knight check that also attacks d4.
puzzles.explanation: The knight lands on e2, checking the black king while attacking the queen. The unique checking move satisfies the fork objective.
puzzles.authorNote: New four-piece fork composition; all legal moves were classified with the chess-rules engine.

puzzles.title: Black's central fork
puzzles.prompt: Black to move: find the knight check that attacks the queen too.
hints: The white king and queen sit on the same file.
Jump to f4 to attack d5 and d3.
puzzles.explanation: The knight checks the king on d5 and attacks the queen on d3. Every legal response leaves the queen attacked.
puzzles.authorNote: New four-piece fork composition; the exact accepted move set was verified.

puzzles.title: The d-file double attack
puzzles.prompt: White to move: fork the king and queen with a checking knight move.
hints: The king is on b6 and the queen on c3.
A knight check from d5 attacks both targets.
puzzles.explanation: The knight checks the king on b6 while attacking the queen on c3. The king must respond, leaving the queen attacked.
puzzles.authorNote: New four-piece fork composition; the exact accepted move set was verified.

puzzles.title: Fork from the rim
puzzles.prompt: White to move: jump from the edge to fork king and queen.
hints: The queen is on a6 and the king is on d7.
The knight checks from b8 while attacking both pieces.
puzzles.explanation: From b8 the knight checks the king on d7 and attacks the queen on a6. The unique checking fork survives every legal reply.
puzzles.authorNote: New four-piece fork composition; the exact accepted move set was verified.

puzzles.title: Black forks from f4
puzzles.prompt: Black to move: find the knight check that attacks the queen.
hints: The white king is on c5 and the queen on e1.
A jump to d3 forks both targets.
puzzles.explanation: The knight checks the king on c5 and attacks the queen on e1. This is the unique checking fork.
puzzles.authorNote: New four-piece fork composition; the exact accepted move set was verified.

puzzles.title: A knight's double threat
puzzles.prompt: White to move: check the king and attack the queen together.
hints: The black king is on e5 and its queen on e7.
Find the knight check from g6.
puzzles.explanation: The knight checks the king on e5 while attacking the queen on e7. The king must move, leaving the queen attacked.
puzzles.authorNote: New four-piece fork composition; the exact accepted move set was verified.

puzzles.title: Black's e6 fork
puzzles.prompt: Black to move: find the knight move that checks and attacks the queen.
hints: The white king is on c5 and queen on d4.
The knight can fork them from e6.
puzzles.explanation: The knight checks the king on c5 and attacks the queen on d4. The queen remains attacked after every legal response.
puzzles.authorNote: New four-piece fork composition; the exact accepted move set was verified.

puzzles.title: Check and attack h6
puzzles.prompt: White to move: use the knight to check and fork the queen.
hints: The black king is on h4 and the queen on h6.
A knight check from f5 attacks both.
puzzles.explanation: The knight checks the king on h4 while attacking the queen on h6. The forced king response leaves the queen attacked.
puzzles.authorNote: New four-piece fork composition; the exact accepted move set was verified.

puzzles.title: Black's d5 fork
puzzles.prompt: Black to move: check the king and attack the queen with the knight.
hints: The white king is on f4 and queen on c7.
A jump to d5 attacks both pieces.
puzzles.explanation: The knight on d5 checks the king and attacks the queen on c7. The king must answer, so the queen remains vulnerable.
puzzles.authorNote: New four-piece fork composition; the exact accepted move set was verified.

puzzles.title: Fork on d6
puzzles.prompt: White to move: find the knight check that attacks the queen as well.
hints: The black king is on b7 and the queen on e4.
The knight's d6 square attacks both.
puzzles.explanation: The knight checks the king on b7 and attacks the queen on e4. The checking fork is unique.
puzzles.authorNote: New four-piece fork composition; the exact accepted move set was verified.

puzzles.title: Black's c6 fork
puzzles.prompt: Black to move: fork the white king and queen with a knight check.
hints: The targets are on a5 and d4.
The knight can reach c6 with check.
puzzles.explanation: The knight checks the king on a5 and attacks the queen on d4. The king must move while the queen remains attacked.
puzzles.authorNote: New four-piece fork composition; the exact accepted move set was verified.

puzzles.title: A fork from the a-file
puzzles.prompt: Black to move: give check while attacking the queen.
hints: The knight can jump toward the white king and queen.
Find the check from c2 that also attacks d4.
puzzles.explanation: The knight checks the king on a1 and attacks the queen on d4. The king has to respond, leaving the queen attacked.
puzzles.authorNote: New four-piece fork composition; the exact accepted move set was verified.
